newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Looting scare causes stir in Zaire's capital.
newsitem.headline: Looting scare causes stir in Zaire's capital.

text.p: A looting scare caused panic in a district of Zaire's jittery capital Kinshasa when soldiers seized 16 vehicles from a Belgian car company, reviving memories of vicious nationwide army pillaging in 1991 and 1993.

But the government, conscious of public fears of a similar outbreak if the army's fortunes take another turn for the worse aginst rebels in the east, played down Thursday's incident, linking it to a lost court case and saying it got out of hand.
"I don't think we can talk of looting," Justice Minister Tshibabwa Ashila Pashi told state radio. "Each time there is an incident everyone thinks that it is looting."
The radio said the incident caused panic in the Kingabwa neighbourhood on the road to Kinshasa's international airport.

The minister said soldiers usurped the role of gendarmes, designated to act a bailiffs. "Unfortunately these elements, who we have yet to identify precisely, committed what we can consider barbaric acts."
He said they encircled the neighbourhood, entered the company compound and stole vehicles and communications gear.
Sources close to the company blamed the presidential guard.

On the war front, comments from defence ministry officials and rebel radio pointed to rebel activity on several fronts -- notably in or near the economically vital mining provinces of Shaba and Kasai.
But a ministry spokesman said on Thursday that the strategic town of Kisangani, the army's headquarters in the war zone and a prime target of the rebels, was quiet.

Military analysts say that the combined forces of the notoriously ill-disciplined Zairean army's better troops, Serb mercenaries and allied Rwandan Hutu hardliners might slow a rebel advance on the city. The army, which has helicopter gunships, has sown minefields around the city.

On the diplomatic front, France called for a "security framework" for Zaire -- code words for a multinational force -- but diplomats said its European Union partners responded coolly. Kenya downgraded a planned March 19 mini summit on Zaire to a preparatory meeting for a full regional summit later.
Zaire's veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko remained in France. He has spent most of his time in Europe since surgery for prostate cancer in Switerland in August.
Shaba and Kasai and copper, diamonds or other minerals mined there are at the heart of Zaire's economy and state revenues.

The defence ministry has reported reinforcements being sent to defend the capital of the diamond-rich Kasai. "We have sent reinforcements to Mbuji Mayi as a precaution against any attacks by the enemy there," a spokesman said.
It said government naval units clashed on Wednesday with rebels advancing south in dug-out canoes on Lake Tanganyika in Shaba towards the port of Moliro.
In Geneva, the U.N. said its special human rights investigator would visit Zaire to probe allegations of massacres of Hutu refugees by the Tutsi-led rebels.
Tired and frightened Rwandan Hutu refugees have been limping into the town of Ubundu on the Zaire River upstream from Kisangani, with tales of the weak and sick dying on the way.

U.N. refugee officials say about 75,000 refugees had reached Ubundu, talking of pushing further west. Most fled Rwanda fearing reprisals in 1994 after the genocide by Hutu hardliners of minority Tutsis.
